report_name: xpl0itrs Group Claims 6.1TB Data Theft from Italy's Gruppo Spaggiari

threat_actors.name: xpl0itrs
threat_actors.description: An emerging extortion group that appeared in 2026. It operates on a double-extortion model, focusing on data theft and public blackmail rather than data encryption. The group claimed responsibility for the data breach against Gruppo Spaggiari Parma.
threat_actors.goals: To extort money from victims by stealing sensitive data and threatening to leak it.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Considered the most probable initial access vector, targeting a vulnerability in the 'Modulistica Smart Bergantini' web form component of Gruppo Spaggiari.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: After gaining initial access, the attackers likely located and exfiltrated data from the underlying databases or file stores, which may have been cloud-based.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: The alleged 6.1 TB of data was transferred from the victim's network to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

attack_patterns.name: Financial Theft
attack_patterns.description: The xpl0itrs group is engaging in extortion by attempting to sell the stolen data for $50,000 and threatening to leak it after failed negotiations.

identities.name: Gruppo Spaggiari Parma
identities.description: A leading Italian developer of school administration software, including the 'ClasseViva' platform. It was the primary victim of the data breach claimed by the xpl0itrs group.

identities.name: Italian Schools
identities.description: Over 3,000 Italian schools were reportedly affected by the data breach, with sensitive data of students and teachers being compromised.

infrastructure.name: xpl0itrs Exfiltration Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Attacker-controlled infrastructure used to receive the 6.1 TB of data exfiltrated from Gruppo Spaggiari's systems.
